A KeePassXC account keeps your vaults in sync between KeePassXC on your computers and KeePass Web in your browser, and lets you share vaults with other people and with your organization. Everything is encrypted on your devices, with your master password and a Secret Key that only you have. The account server and the sync server only ever store encrypted vaults and keys sealed to their members, so they can’t read your passwords. An account is optional: KeePassXC works without one exactly as it always has.

Ways to Use KeePassXC

The first time you start KeePassXC, the start screen offers three ways to use it:

Your choice is remembered, so later launches skip the start screen; Account → Sign In or Create Account… brings it back.

Choice What it does

Sign in / Create account

Your vaults live in your KeePassXC account and open with your account’s master password. They sync automatically and can be shared.

Use my own sync server

Your databases sync with a KeePassXC Sync Server you run yourself. Enter the server’s URL and a pairing code from another of your devices or from the server’s admin; new databases are then set up to sync with that server. Each database keeps its own master password. See KeePassXC Sync Server.

Use without an account

Database files on your computer, with their own master passwords. Nothing leaves your computer unless you set up a sync yourself.

Creating an Account

  1. On the start screen, click Create account.

  2. Enter your email address and choose a master password. Nobody can reset your master password, not even the server’s operators, so choose one you will remember. Click Change server only if you use a KeePassXC account server other than the default one.

  3. KeePassXC creates your Secret Key on this computer and shows it once. Click Save Emergency Kit… to save or print the Emergency Kit, a PDF with your email, the server, your Secret Key, and a space to write down your master password, and keep it somewhere safe.

  4. Confirm that you saved the Emergency Kit to finish.

Important

You need your master password and your Secret Key to sign in on a new device. If you lose both your devices and your Emergency Kit, your vaults can’t be recovered.

Signing In

On the start screen, enter your email and master password and click Sign in. The first time on a device, also click First time on this device? Enter your Secret Key and enter the Secret Key from your Emergency Kit; afterwards the device keeps it. If you turned on two-step verification, enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.

Once you are signed in, your account’s vaults all open at once, with no password of their own. They are listed in the database picker under Personal and under the name of each organization you belong to, and the account button at the far right of the header shows who is signed in.

Locking and Quick Unlock

Locking a vault, or Account → Lock Account, locks the account and closes all of its vaults. Account → Unlock Account… asks for your master password and opens them again.

When Quick Unlock is available (Touch ID on macOS, Windows Hello on Windows, or your system password through Polkit on Linux) and turned on under Tools → Settings → Security, Account → Quick Unlock Account unlocks the account without typing the master password. The keys it needs stay in memory only: they are dropped when you sign out or quit KeePassXC.

Vaults

Account → New Vault… creates a vault. It can belong to you or to an organization you manage; a vault of an organization opens for all of its owners and admins, and you can share it with other members afterwards.

Vaults sync automatically, the same way as with a sync server (see Automatic Sync and Conflicts): after each save, when changes arrive from your other devices, and when you come back online.

Moving a Database to Your Account

To bring an existing database into your account, open and unlock it, then select Account → Move Database to Account… and enter a name for the vault. A copy of the database becomes a personal vault, encrypted with a new vault key instead of its master password, and syncs with your account from then on. The database file itself isn’t changed.

Sharing a Vault

Select a vault, then Account → Share Vault…:

  1. Enter the email address of the person to share with and click Look up.

  2. Check their fingerprint with them, for example over the phone: they see the same fingerprint in their own app. Only share when it matches.

  3. Choose their access and click Share:

    • Read only – they can open the vault and copy from it.

    • Can edit – they can also change its entries.

    • Can manage – they can also share it with others and remove members.

To change someone’s access select them and click Change. Removing a member gives the vault a new key, sealed only to the remaining members, so that what the removed member kept can’t open the vault’s future versions.

Organizations

Account → Organizations, Service Accounts and Audit Log… opens the organization settings. Click New organization… to create one; you become its owner. For each organization you can manage:

  • Members – Invite people by email with the role Owner, Admin, or Member. The invitation is valid for 7 days; they accept it with Account → Accept Invitation… by pasting the link or code from the email. An owner or admin then checks their fingerprint and clicks Confirm… to choose the vaults they can open. Owners and admins get every vault of the organization. You can also change a member’s role, remove them (their vaults get new keys), or select yourself and click Leave… to leave the organization.

  • Service accounts – Accounts for a CI job, a server, or a Kubernetes cluster rather than a person. Give a service account access to vaults (Read only or Can edit), then click Issue secret… to create a token for it. The token is shown only once: copy it to where it will be used, for example as a CI secret. Each secret can expire on a date, which you can change later with Change expiry…, and can be revoked at any time.

  • Audit log – Who did what and when in the organization, such as sign-ins, shares, and member and service-account changes.

Service account tokens are used by the kpx command line tool, which reads secrets from vaults with references such as kpx read kpx://Production/Database/password or runs a command with secrets in its environment (kpx run --env-file .env — <command>), by kpx connect, a REST server for other programs and Kubernetes, and by the GitHub Action.

Managing Your Account

Account → Manage Account… opens your account page in KeePass Web in your browser; sign in there if it asks. There you can change your email or master password, turn two-step verification on or off, see your devices and sign them out, and download your Emergency Kit again. Changes made there reach KeePassXC on your other devices automatically.

Account → Sign Out signs this device out of your account and closes its vaults. Databases on your computer stay usable.
